summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, chronic diastolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and autoimmune hemolytic anemia, was admitted for altered mental status and fever. He was found to have Listeria monocytogenes bacteremia and meningitis, confirmed by blood and CSF cultures. He was treated with ampicillin and gentamicin, with clinical improvement. MRI revealed a small acute infarct in the right precentral gyrus, but his mental status recovery suggested infection as the primary cause of AMS. He required transfusions for pancytopenia and had stable chronic kidney disease that improved during admission. His home medications were adjusted, including reduction in insulin and atenolol. He was discharged to a rehab facility to complete his antibiotic course and continue rehabilitation.
